patch.value: Two plausible directions: batch the routing assertions into a single CLI invocation, or drive the routing contract from the command registry directly rather than through repeated process spawns. Raising a timeout would hide the sensitivity rather than remove it.
A thirty-five second CLI test fails on timing whenever the machine is busy, so the gate reports red for load rather than for code

The test named installed pm CLI routes --repos values to every fleet command spawns the installed pm binary many times in sequence and takes roughly 30 to 35 seconds on an idle machine. It failed twice today while six packages full gate suites ran in parallel, and passed on the same commit both times when run alone, and also passed on main under the same parallel load conditions in one of the two comparisons. Nothing about the change under review touches the code paths it exercises. A gate that long is load sensitive by construction, so a red result from a parallel sweep cannot be distinguished from a real regression without a second serial run, which costs another half minute every time it happens.
The test either bounds its own runtime independently of machine load, or spawns the CLI once and asserts over the batch rather than once per command, so that a busy machine cannot turn it red

message: Record the load-sensitive CLI routing test

patch.value: The test named installed pm CLI routes --repos values to every fleet command spawns the installed pm binary many times in sequence and takes roughly 30 to 35 seconds on an idle machine. On 2026-08-26 UTC it failed twice while six packages full gate suites ran in parallel, and passed when re-run alone on the same commit. It also passed on main under comparable parallel load. The conclusion is that the test is load sensitive rather than broken, so a red result from a parallel sweep must be re-run in isolation before it is believed.

value.author: claude
value.text: Corrected an internal inconsistency this record carried: the description claimed the commit passed in isolation on both re-runs while the note recorded a single isolated pass among three observations. Those cannot both be right and I cannot re-derive which from the surviving evidence, so both now state only what is defensible - two failures under six-way parallel load, and a pass when re-run alone on the same commit - without asserting a count of isolated re-runs that the records disagree about. Inconsistent evidence is worse than less evidence, because it misleads flake triage.
